newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Tupras still mulls contract for Iraqi oil.
newsitem.headline: Turk Tupras still mulls contract for Iraqi oil.

text.p: Turkey's state-owned oil refiner Tupras said on Tuesday it was still considering signing a contract to buy Iraqi oil after the United Nations gave Iraq clearance to start resuming limited exports.
"Our general manager is abroad for talks and as far as I know the work on this is continuing," a Tupras spokeswoman told Reuters.
"We have no figure for how much we would buy," she said.
Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said earlier that Iraq had sent two contracts to the U.N. Secretary-General that would enable Iraq to sell its oil to international companies.
In a statement carried by the official Iraqi News Agency (INA), Rasheed did not name the purchasers, but said Iraq would give preference to Turkey in selling its oil.
President Saddam Hussein pressed the button that resumed Iraqi oil exports to world markets at 0825 GMT on Tuesday after a six-year break, the official Iraqi News Agency reported.
Tupras has an annual refining capacity of 27.6 million tonnes with refineries in Batman, Izmir and Kirikkale.
Spokesmen for France's Elf Aquitaine and Total, two of the first companies expected to be awarded contracts, said on Monday their firms had not signed deals yet.

The United Nations gave Iraq clearance on Monday to start resuming limited exports of oil, from 0501 GMT on Tuesday, under an "oil-for-food" deal for Iraqis suffering under economic sanctions imposed on Iraq after its invasion of Kuwait in 1990.

Under the U.N. plan, concluded in May but held up by disputes over implementation, Iraq will be able to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian goods.
